newsitem.title: USA: Readers Digest reports fourth quarter loss.
newsitem.headline: Readers Digest reports fourth quarter loss.

text.p: Days after its chief executive quit, beleaguered publishing giant Reader's Digest Association Inc. said Thursday that it lost nearly $23 million in the fourth quarter as it struggled to revamp its businesses.

The fourth quarter loss, which was 22 cents a share, came after the company took pre-tax charges of $35 million to realign its businesses and $29 million to write down bloated inventories in books, music and videos that it sells via direct mail.
The company earned nearly $46 million, or 42 cents a sahre in the year-earlier period.

The publisher also warned that 1998 results would be lower than full-year 1997. "Planned investment in more aggressive publishing and marketing initiatives will contribute to lower fiscal 1998 results," the company said in a statement.
For 1997, Reader's Digest had net income of $133.5 million, or $1.24 a share, versus $80.6 million, or 73 cents a share, in 1996.
The company said it expects to take unspecified charges in the first quarter of 1998 "associated with the realignment of business processes and operations as the plan is finalized."
It expects first quarter results to be "significantly lower" than last year's $34.6 million, or 32 cents a share.

As part of an attempted turnaround, the company has been cutting costs, especially in its European operations, seeking new ways to distribute its products, and tap into a younger market. In April, it announced a $400 million program to boost its business.

On Aug. 11, the company announced that James Schadt, 59, had resigned as chairman and was replaced by his predecessor, George Grune, 68, who took the company public and guided it through a period of considerable growth.
While analysts had praised Schadt for his turnaround plan, they said progress had not been quick enough. Wall Street, unhappy with the sagging stock price, had put pressure on the board.
"It's a very big tanker to turn around," said one industry analyst.
The quarterly results were released after the stock market closed on Thursday. Shares were unchanged at $27.56 on the New York Stock Exchange.
